questions.q: The test scores of five students are $75, 80, 85, 90, 95$. What is the mean score?
What is the median of the data set: $14, 8, 22, 11, 19, 5, 17$?
questions.answer: Order the numbers: $5, 8, 11, 14, 17, 19, 22$. The middle value (4th of 7) is $14$.

questions.q: The average of $4$ numbers is $15$. If a fifth number is added, the new average becomes $18$. What is the fifth number?
questions.answer: Original sum $= 4 \times 15 = 60$. New sum $= 5 \times 18 = 90$. The fifth number $= 90 - 60 = 30$.

questions.q: A fair six-sided die is rolled. What is the probability of obtaining an even number or a number greater than $4$?
questions.answer: Even numbers: $\{2, 4, 6\}$. Numbers $> 4$: $\{5, 6\}$. Union: $\{2, 4, 5, 6\}$ (4 outcomes). Probability $= \frac{4}{6} = \frac{2}{3}$.

questions.q: A bag contains $4$ red marbles, $6$ blue marbles, and $5$ green marbles. If one marble is drawn at random, what is the probability that it is NOT blue?
Two coins are tossed simultaneously. What is the probability of getting at least one Head?
questions.answer: Sample space: $\{HH, HT, TH, TT\}$ (4 outcomes). At least one head: $\{HH, HT, TH\}$ (3 outcomes). Probability $= \frac{3}{4}$.

sections.heading: Section 3: Circular Pie Charts & Sector Percentages

questions.q: In a circle graph representing a family's budget, the angle representing housing expenses is $90^\circ$. What percentage of the budget is spent on housing?
questions.answer: A full circle is $360^\circ$. Housing percentage $= \frac{90^\circ}{360^\circ} \times 100\% = \frac{1}{4} \times 100\% = 25\%$.

questions.q: A circle graph represents a company's sales of $720,000$ SAR. If the food sector has a central angle of $60^\circ$, what is the sales value of the food sector?
If a sector of a circle graph represents $40\%$ of the total, what is its central angle?
A restaurant menu offers $4$ appetizers, $5$ main courses, and $3$ desserts. How many different $3$-course meals can a customer choose?
questions.answer: By the fundamental counting principle: $4 \times 5 \times 3 = 60$ distinct meals.

questions.q: How many $3$-digit numbers can be formed using the digits $\{1, 2, 3, 4, 5\}$ if repetition of digits is NOT allowed?
questions.answer: Hundreds digit: $5$ choices. Tens digit: $4$ choices. Units digit: $3$ choices. Total numbers $= 5 \times 4 \times 3 = 60$.

questions.q: In a meeting of $6$ people, if everyone shakes hands with everyone else exactly once, how many handshakes take place?
